The Bruins had been ranked at No. 6 coming into this past week. item.title: 49ers' Mac Jones wouldn't have minded a trade. A tradeoff? He gets to start vs. Seattle
item.description: Quarterback Mac Jones started eight games for the 49ers last season while Brock Purdy was hurt. Jones will get the start Sunday against the Seahawks while Purdy recovers from an ankle injury. (Ryan Sun/Associated Press) Mac Jones will start for a franchise Sunday that he was at least halfway hoping would get rid of him less than three weeks ago. On Friday, when asked about the interest he generated before the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10, the San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback was candid. Did Jones think it sounded more appealing to start for a playoff contender in need of a QB rather than keep collecting dust behind Brock Purdy ? "Yeah, definitely have thought about it," Jones said. "And I was just glad that the deadline was over because I got to move forward." On Sunday, Jones will move into the starting lineup with Purdy sidelined with a sprained left ankle. And Jones will have a chance to show why the 49ers have declined to deal him after his brilliant 2025 relief work made him an appealing trade target. After playing 20 mop-up snaps this season, Jones' first real action will be a real challenge: He'll face the Seahawks' top-ranked defense at Levi's Stadium with rain in the forecast. Jones, 28, noted he long ago gained NFL experience playing in wet conditions against a formidable foe. On Oct. 3, 2021, in his fourth career start as a rookie, Jones faced Tampa Bay, then the defending Super Bowl champions, and QB Tom Brady in Brady's only game against New England, his employer for his first 20 seasons. Jones completed 31 of 40 passes for 275 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in a 19-17 loss in a downpour. "That was like the game of the century," Jones said, laughing. "And I wasn't freaking out about the rain. I just went out there and played. So that's what I'm going to do this time." Jones' work last season gives the 49ers confidence he can deliver on the promise. Jones went 5-3, ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage (69.6), 12th in yards per attempt (7.4) and 13th in passer rating (97.4) among the 36 QBs who had at least 200 pass attempts. In his final start, a 42-26 loss to the Rams, he became the third QB in franchise history to complete 30-plus passes with a completion percentage of at least 80%, joining Steve Young and Jeff Garcia. In his penultimate start, a 34-24 road win against the Giants, he completed 19 of 24 passes, and he joined Young and Joe Montana as the only QBs in franchise history to complete at least 14 consecutive passes to start a game. item.title: USWNT winners and losers: Emma Hayes' side clinch 2027 World Cup berth in 8-0 rout of El Salvador as Ashley Sanchez makes roster statement with hat trick
item.description: Ashley Sanchez Ashley Sanchez stole the show with a hat trick, while Lily Yohannes pulled the strings in midfield as the USWNT secured World Cup qualification in emphatic fashion. The U.S. Women's National Team took care of business against El Salvador in Mansfield, Texas, on Friday night, cruising to an 8-0 win and securing a direct berth at the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup. It took just nine minutes for the U.S. to open the floodgates, with center back Kennedy Wesley making a late run into the box to put the Americans on the scoreboard. Despite committing six defenders to the back line, El Salvador struggled to contain the USWNT in the box. The U.S. scored six more goals before halftime, with Ashley Sanchez leading the way with a hat trick. The second half was a quieter affair, but Croix Bethune added an eighth as the Americans continued to dominate, finishing the match with 78 percent possession compared to El Salvador's 22 percent. Emma Hayes' side can now confidently check World Cup qualification off their list. And while the USWNT's attacking display stole the show, the Americans were equally commanding defensively, not allowing a single shot on target. GOAL looks at the Winners & Losers from Texas Health Mansfield Stadium in Mansfield, Texas. WINNER: Ashley Sanchez The pressure has been on Sanchez to deliver for the national team. The midfielder enjoyed the best NWSL season of her career, scoring 20 goals for the North Carolina Courage and earning league MVP honors. Sanchez earned her second straight national team call-up, and despite limited minutes in two promising appearances against Spain, she still had work to do to secure a spot on the World Cup roster. On Friday, Sanchez took her role in midfield in stride and executed it almost flawlessly. She led the U.S. with a hat trick, and none of her three goals were simple tap-ins. She made quick runs to the far post, evaded pressure and used delicate touches in tight spaces to create narrow windows to shoot. There was no shortage of standout attacking performances for the USWNT on Friday night, but Sanchez's was the most impressive. If she can continue translating her club form to the international stage, she'll be difficult for Hayes to leave off her World Cup roster. LOSER: El Salvador's backline El Salvador played with six in the back against the United States in the Concacaf W Championship. El Salvador knew they had a massive test ahead of them against the four-time World Cup champions. Between incisive through balls, quick one- and two-touch passing and clever movement in the box, the USWNT exposed the shortcomings of El Salvador's defensive approach. item.title: ‘In a weird way’: Mason Rudolph shares how the Aaron Rodgers drama actually helped Steelers beat Broncos
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers capped off a very difficult week with a fine win over the Denver Broncos. The drama surrounding Aaron Rodgers, who was released earlier this week, dominated the headlines, and many felt that would have an impact on the team. However, the Steelers were incredibly dominant, beating the Broncos 27-5. Mason Rudolph says the Aaron Rodgers ‘adversity’ brought the Steelers together Mason Rudolph hadn’t been involved in first-team reps all week, which is why he had to put in extra work on Thursday ahead of Friday’s game. The quarterback, who took over Rodgers’ role, definitely played his part, delivering a clean, efficient and turnover-free game-manager performance. Unsurprisingly, the questions after the game were always going to be dominated by the Rodgers saga during the week. Rudolph was asked about it too, and he claimed that the controversy helped, as it brought the team a lot closer ahead of the win against the Broncos. He said on Prime Video: “It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented, nothing I’ve ever been through and probably the same for all my teammates. “We’re so proud of the way we turned the page on Wednesday, and the veteran leadership – Cameron Heyward, Jalen Ramsey, T. J. Watt – really led us forward.” Rudolph further added: “I think the leadership council just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy. And I think, in a weird way, you know, the adversity brought us probably closer together. And I think we’ll just keep carrying that into week after week.” The 31-year-old hadn’t started a game for over a year, so the pressure was on for him to deliver after taking Rodgers’ place against the Broncos. Rudolph finished the game with nine of 15 passes completed (60.0%) for 142 yards and one touchdown. He took a sack for a 12-yard loss, which was really the only blemish in his performance, while posting a 113.8 passer rating. All in all, it was a fine outing for the Steelers after what has been a tough week. We’re sure Rudolph and everyone else will be delighted with how the game panned out. item.description: Ashley Sanchez needed just six minutes and 27 seconds to score a hat trick, helping the United States women’s national team dismantle El Salvador in the quarterfinals of the Concacaf W Championship on Friday, securing a place at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. For all the attacking power head coach Emma Hayes assembled in her starting lineup, it was her center backs who got the scoring underway first in front of a crowd of 6,595 at at Texas Health Stadium in Mansfield, Texas. Kennedy Wesley opened the scoring in the ninth minute, finishing Mallory Swanson’s cross. Tierna Davidson doubled the lead at the half-hour mark, finishing another Swanson pass, just before Swanson added a third goal moments later. Then came the Sanchez show. The North Carolina Courage midfielder, coming off an MVP-winning NWSL season with a golden boot under her belt, scored in the 37th minute, and again in the 39th and completed a hat trick in the 43rd. Sophia Wilson set up one goal while Alyssa Thompson provided the other two assists. Wilson wrapped the first-half scoring in the 45th minute, finishing a pass from captain Lindsey Heaps to give the U.S. a 7-0 lead in the first 45 minutes. For Sanchez, Friday night in Mansfield, Texas, was the continuation of a remarkable comeback. Before returning to the USWNT in October against Spain, the 27-year-old had gone 710 days without a call up to the national team. Her goal against Spain in Philadelphia, Penn. was her first international goal since 2022, when she scored against Costa Rica in the previous Concacaf W Championship, helping the USWNT qualify for the 2023 Women’s World Cup and the 2024 Paris Olympics. Hayes made a handful of substitutions in the second half, bringing Croix Bethune, Jadyn Shaw, Michelle Cooper and Sam Coffey in for Wilson, Swanson, Thompson, Lily Yohannes. Bethune, who won NWSL’s midfielder of the year award and broke the single season assist record before lifting the NWSL trophy with Kansas City Current last weekend, scored the eighth goal in the 80th minute, finishing Heaps’ assist with a smooth placement into the back of the net. But perhaps as interesting as the scoreline was Hayes’ selection for the first qualifying match of her tenure since winning the gold medal in Paris in 2024. With Trinity Rodman unavailable due to shoulder injury, Hayes opted for a starting XI that relied mostly on NWSL standouts: attacking trio of Swanson, Wilson and Alyssa Thompson, with Yohannes, Sanchez and Heaps in midfield, Emily Fox, Gisele Thompson as fullbacks, Davidson and Wesley as center backs and Seattle Reign’s Claudia Dickey in goal. item.title: Somers ends a magical season for Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football in state semifinals
item.description: The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team's season ended with a state semifinal loss to Somers on Friday in Middletown. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - The Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake football team put in plenty of work this season, which resulted in the Spartans tripling their win total from 2025. But on Friday evening, the Spartans' incredible turnaround season came to a crushing conclusion. The Spartans could not get anything going of consequence during the first half of the their Class A state semifinal showdown against top-ranked Somers. Meanwhile, the Tuskers produced touchdowns on all four of their offensive series in the first half and cruised to a comfortable 35-7 victory at Middletown High School. Ty Starr made sure the Spartans were not shut out when the senior took a handoff and swept off the left side for a 56-yard touchdown run with 18 seconds left in the game. "They are a really good team. We played our hearts out - everyone throughout the team, and that is that," BH-BL senior linebacker Logan Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, they won. Good for them. Have them go win it all. We fell short." Somers (13-0) is a program with four Class A state titles to its credit since 2016, including three straight championships from 2022 to 2024. The Tuskers proved too tough for BH-BL to contain during the first half as the Section 1 champions produced touchdown drives covering 62, 81, 98 and 61 yards in establishing a 28-0 halftime cushion. "We always talk about life. Life isn't perfect," BH-BL coach Kevin DeBonis said. "We just lost to a very good team. We came out uncharacteristic. We stubbed our toes with assignments. That's what happens. Unfortunately, they exposed that. They are a very good team. It is hard to go down like that. It was sort of an avalanche early on." Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake, making its 11th state playoff appearance since 2006, hasn't reached the final since claiming the program's first state championship in 2012. This season's squad ended up matching the program record for wins in a season with 12, a standard first established in 2009 and matched by the state championship squad from 14 years ago. "We had the biggest bounce back (season) of my life," Tomlinson said. "At the end of the day, we won 12 games. If we didn't do that, I would be a little bit more upset." After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
